findings.finding: Navigating to https://www.google.com and https://google.com produced a 'ready' status but a visually blank content area. This is Google's own X-Frame-Options/CSP frame-ancestors policy blocking embedding in any iframe from any origin (standard behavior everywhere, including Safari/Chrome), not a Veil-specific defect. Confirmed the underlying rendering pipeline works by loading https://en.wikipedia.org, which rendered real page content.
findings.recommended_change: Consider a short in-app note near the WebView (or in its documentation) that some sites refuse to be framed by design and will show a blank area even when status is 'ready', so this isn't mistaken for a bug during future manual passes.

findings.finding: Repeated 'ready' entries appeared in the decision log for the same or near-duplicate URLs (e.g. https://www.google.com and https://google.com) during this session's manual testing, consistent with the same non-blocking finding recorded in the previous validation pass at commit 3e44139.
findings.recommended_change: Deduplicate equivalent consecutive decisions in a later bounded observability refinement (carried forward from the prior validation record; not yet addressed).

decision_reason: The packaged macOS application launches, renders the adult gate and Browser/WebView surfaces, allows HTTPS navigation (verified with real content rendering via Wikipedia), blocks HTTP navigation with a visible policy reason, keeps downloads blocked and the sandbox active, and records both allowed and blocked decisions in the log. Two non-blocking findings were recorded above: an expected third-party anti-framing behavior (Google) that could read as a bug without context, and a previously-known decision-log duplication issue that has not yet been fixed.
